_comment: Candidate addresses for the seed-verify method (D) and the starting frontier for the transaction-sampling crawl (C). Nothing in this file is asserted to be true. Every entry is a CANDIDATE that the scanner independently verifies against mainnet RPC; candidates that turn out not to exist, not to be Token-2022, or not to carry a TransferHook are dropped and never appear in the census. Sources are recorded so a reviewer can judge selection bias.
_bias_warning: This list is not a sample of anything. It is whatever a small manual search turned up. Findings derived from it may not be generalised to the mainnet population.

candidateMints.note: PayPal USD (PYUSD). Widely documented as a Token-2022 mint.
candidateMints.source: well-known Token-2022 mint

candidateMints.note: BonkEarn. Cited in a web search result as a mainnet Token-2022 transfer-hook example; included so the claim gets checked rather than repeated.
candidateMints.source: web search claim, unverified at time of listing

candidateMints.note: USDC. Legacy SPL Token, included as a negative control — the scanner must reject it.
candidateMints.source: negative control

candidateMints.note: $HUKT, the token of a site advertising itself as a Token-2022 transfer-hook framework. Included because the association invites the assumption that it carries a hook; the scan is what decides.
candidateMints.source: hukt.fun, claim unverified at time of listing

candidateMints.note: Listed by hukt.fun as its demonstration mint. Retained deliberately: a reproduction run should observe that this account does not exist on mainnet, which is itself the check working.
candidateMints.source: hukt.fun, claim unverified at time of listing

candidateMints.note: Confirmed to carry a TransferHook extension. Promoted to a seed so coverage is monotonic across runs — transaction sampling walks a different window each time and would otherwise drop it.
